1	# Your role: Backend
2	
3	Own the Backend layer of the synthetic ticket board.
4	
5	> **Human reading this:** run `/grill-my-role` in your AI editor, or paste
6	> to your agent: _"Read .grill-with-me/MY-ROLE.md and follow it."_ Then just answer the
7	> questions — about ten minutes. Everything below is addressed to the agent.
8	
9	## What you own
10	- src/api.ts
11	
12	## Before we start
13	Read `grill/PROJECT.md`, any `grill/*-spec.md` files your teammates have
14	already committed, and the repo you are standing in.
15	
16	## The grill
17	
18	Interview me relentlessly about MY LAYER ONLY — the "Backend" role —
19	until we reach a shared understanding of what I am building and what I need
20	from the other roles. Walk down each branch of the decision tree, resolving
21	dependencies between decisions one by one. For each question, provide your
22	recommended answer. Ask one question at a time — multiple questions at once
23	is bewildering.
24	Give the recommendation as a statement, then request one decision. Do not
25	append a second question about setup, the next topic, or whether to ask another
26	question; defer those choices to a later turn.
27	
28	If a fact can be found in the repo, look it up rather than asking me. The
29	decisions are mine.
30	
31	Prefer questions that reference something real: code that already exists in
32	this repo, or something a teammate wrote in their spec. If my answer
33	contradicts a teammate's committed spec, point at the exact line and ask
34	which of us should change.
35	Only call it a contradiction when the two statements are incompatible.
36	A teammate omitting a detail (such as a column default) does not reject it.
37	
38	Make sure we cover:
39	- Missing ticket response
40	- Close operation boundary
41	
42	Keep a short running summary of what you have understood so far, and show it
43	to me every few questions so I can correct drift early.
44	
45	Keep observed repo behavior, teammate commitments, my explicit answers, and
46	your recommendations distinct. A recommendation becomes my decision only when
47	I explicitly accept it. Saying "I'm done" ends the interview; it does not
48	accept an unanswered recommendation or authorize you to choose its details.
49	Who supplies a test, assertion, or other input does not settle its file
50	location or exclude it from another role's owned file. Keep that placement
51	unresolved unless it was explicitly agreed; do not add the exclusion as a
52	decision merely from the supplying role.
53	
54	## When I say I'm done
55	
56	Write `grill/backend-spec.md` containing EXACTLY these five headings once
57	each, in this order, outside code fences. Individual sections may be empty;
58	a spec empty under every heading is invalid:
59	
60	## Scope
61	## What I own
62	## What I need from other roles
63	## Decisions made
64	## Still unclear
65	
66	Under each heading, be concrete: name endpoints as METHOD /path with request
67	and response shapes, name tables and columns with types, name files by path.
68	"An endpoint that returns items" is useless; `POST /api/rank` returning
69	`{ trails: { id: string; shadeScore: number }[] }` is what the contract
70	needs. Do not invent agreements I did not make — anything not yet agreed
71	belongs under "Still unclear".
72	
73	Describe existing code as observed behavior, not as a decision to preserve or
74	replace it. Record only explicitly chosen changes under "Decisions made".
75	Do not choose new function return shapes, status handling, retry behavior,
76	rendering, or refresh mechanisms just to make the spec concrete. If my answer
77	does not specify one, keep that detail under "Still unclear". For example,
78	"reload" alone does not agree a full page reload or a particular fetch/result
79	shape. State dependencies under "What I need from other roles" as requests
80	until the relevant role has agreed; also list their pending agreement under
81	"Still unclear". Do not claim a teammate approved or implemented a request.
82	
83	Before writing, check concrete claims in EVERY section, including "Scope"
84	and "What I own". An endpoint's ownership does not settle its HTTP status,
85	request body, or pagination. Conventional defaults such as GET returning 200
86	or POST having no body are not agreements. A call site omitting a body or a
87	stub accepting no pagination arguments is only observed behavior; label it
88	with its file path. Each transport rule needs my explicit answer or an
89	existing teammate agreement. Otherwise leave that rule under "Still unclear",
90	even when the response shape and endpoint path are already agreed.
91	
92	Run `npx grill-with-me check-spec grill/backend-spec.md` after writing it.
93	If validation fails, correct the structure or report the missing decisions
94	before telling me to commit. Surface thin-section warnings; never invent
95	agreements just to make a section longer.

I've read the role instructions, project context, the frontend spec, and the repo. Two notes before we start:

- `grill/CONTRACT.md` doesn't exist, so we're in the grilling phase.
- `node .eval-cli/grill.mjs contract-status` failed: `Cannot find module ...\.eval-cli\grill.mjs` — that CLI isn't present in this checkout. I'm reporting that rather than trying another path. It doesn't block the interview.

**What the repo already shows (observed, not decided):**
- `src/api.ts:1` — `paths = { list: "/api/tickets", close: "/api/tickets/:id/close" }`
- `src/api.ts:2` — `listTickets()` returns `{ tickets: [{ id: "t1", title: "Demo", closed: false }] }` (hardcoded, no args)
- `src/api.ts:3` — `closeTicket(id)` returns `{ id, closed: true }` (no DB, no lookup)
- `db/schema.sql:1` — `tickets (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, closed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE)`
- `src/auth.ts:1` — `sessionPolicy()` returns `'not yet agreed'`
- Frontend committed (`grill/frontend-spec.md`): reads `response.tickets` from `GET /api/tickets`, asks Backend for `POST /api/tickets/:id/close`, decided no optimistic updates and "reload the list after a successful close."

---

**Question 1 of the grill — the close operation boundary.**

Right now `closeTicket(id)` in `src/api.ts:3` is pure: it echoes `{ id, closed: true }` without ever touching `tickets.closed`. That means nothing persists, so the frontend's "reload the list after a successful close" would show the ticket still open.

My recommendation: `POST /api/tickets/:id/close` owns the state change end-to-end inside `src/api.ts` — a single `UPDATE tickets SET closed = TRUE WHERE id = ?` — with no separate service or repository layer for this demo, and `src/api.ts` is the only file that issues that write.

Do you accept that the close endpoint performs the `tickets.closed` write itself in `src/api.ts`?
